decision.explanation: The equation gives tan(2x−π/6)=√3/3, so 2x−π/6=π/6+kπ and x=π/6+kπ/2. In the given interval, the ascending solutions are π/6, 2π/3, 7π/6, and 5π/3. Thus x₂·x₃=(2π/3)(7π/6)=7π²/9.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Consider the equation $3\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-\frac{\pi }{6})-\sqrt{3}=0$ for $0\le x<2\pi .$ Given that the exact solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}$ and ${x}_{4}$ are written in ascending order, what is the value of ${x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-\frac{\pi }{6})-\sqrt{3} & =0 \\ 3\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-\frac{\pi }{6}) & =\sqrt{3} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-\frac{\pi }{6}) & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-\frac{\pi }{6} & =\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation above for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =\frac{\pi }{6}+\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi  \\ 2x & =\frac{\pi }{3}+n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{n\pi }{2}+\frac{\pi }{6} \\ x & =\frac{(3n+1)\pi }{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=\frac{\pi }{6}$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x=\frac{2\pi }{3}$

- Setting $n=2$ gives $x=\frac{7\pi }{6}$

- Setting $n=3$ gives $x=\frac{5\pi }{3}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$ So, the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4}$ (written in ascending order) are

$$
x=\frac{\pi }{6},\frac{2\pi }{3},\frac{7\pi }{6},\frac{5\pi }{3}.
$$

Finally, since ${x}_{2}=\frac{2\pi }{3}$ and ${x}_{3}=\frac{7\pi }{6},$ we have

$$
{x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}=\frac{2\pi }{3}\cdot \frac{7\pi }{6}=\frac{7{\pi }^{2}}{9}.
$$

x=π6,2π3,7π6,5π3.

x2⋅x3=2π3⋅7π6=7π29.

Question 2

Consider the equation tan⁡(3x−π4)=1 for 0≤x<π. If the exact solutions x1,x2 and x3 are written in ascending order, what is the value of x2⋅x3?

a
−5π212
b
−5π22
c
5π12
d
5π6
e
5π212
Submit

decision.explanation: Since tan(θ)=1 when θ=π/4+nπ, we have 3x−π/4=π/4+nπ, giving x=π/6+nπ/3. The solutions in 0≤x<π are π/6, π/2, and 5π/6. Therefore x₂·x₃=(π/2)(5π/6)=5π²/12.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: Consider the equation $\operatorname{tan}⁡(3x-\frac{\pi }{4})=1$ for $0\le x<\pi .$ If the exact solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ are written in ascending order, what is the value of ${x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}?$
after.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}3x-\frac{\pi }{4} & =\frac{\pi }{4}+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation above for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3x & =\frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{\pi }{4}+n\pi  \\ 3x & =\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{6}+\frac{n\pi }{3} \\ x & =\frac{(2n+1)\pi }{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0\le x<\pi .$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=\frac{\pi }{6}$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x=\frac{\pi }{2}$

- Setting $n=2$ gives $x=\frac{5\pi }{6}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0\le x<\pi .$ So, the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4}$ (written in ascending order) are

$$
x=\frac{\pi }{6},\,\frac{\pi }{2},\,\frac{5\pi }{6}
$$

Finally, since ${x}_{2}=\frac{\pi }{2}$ and ${x}_{3}=\frac{5\pi }{6},$ we have

$$
{x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}=\frac{\pi }{2}\cdot \frac{5\pi }{6}=\frac{5{\pi }^{2}}{12}.
$$

x=π6,π2,5π6

x2⋅x3=π2⋅5π6=5π212.

Question 3
?

Given that x1 and x2 are the exact solutions to the equation 3tan⁡(2x−7π3)+3=0 for 0≤x<π, what is the value of x1⋅x2?

a
13π576
b
−13π224
c
13π2576
d
13π24
e
−13π2576
Submit

decision.explanation: Dividing by √3 gives tan(2x−7π/3)=−1. Thus 2x−7π/3=−π/4+nπ, so x=25π/24+nπ/2. The two solutions in 0≤x<π are π/24 and 13π/24. Their product is 13π²/576.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: Given that ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the exact solutions to the equation $\sqrt{3}\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-\frac{7\pi }{3})+\sqrt{3}=0$ for $0\le x<\pi ,$ what is the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \sqrt{3}\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-\frac{7\pi }{3})+\sqrt{3}=0 \\  & \sqrt{3}\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-\frac{7\pi }{3})=-\sqrt{3} \\  & \operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-\frac{7\pi }{3})=-1\end{aligned}
$$

We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-\frac{7\pi }{3} & =-\frac{\pi }{4}+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation above for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =\frac{7\pi }{3}-\frac{\pi }{4}+n\pi  \\ 2x & =\frac{25\pi }{12}+n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{25\pi }{24}+\frac{n\pi }{2} \\ x & =\frac{(12n+25)\pi }{24}.\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0\le x<\pi .$

- Setting $n=-2$ gives $x=\frac{\pi }{24}$

- Setting $n=-1$ gives $x=\frac{13\pi }{24}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0\le x<\pi .$ So, the solutions are $x=\frac{\pi }{24},\frac{13\pi }{24}.$

Finally, 

$$
{x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}=\frac{\pi }{24}\cdot \frac{13\pi }{24}=\frac{13{\pi }^{2}}{576}.
$$

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: Given that ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the exact solutions to the equation $\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{x}{2})=1$ for $-2\pi \le x<2\pi ,$ what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
after.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{2} & =\frac{\pi }{4}+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation above for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{2} & =\frac{\pi }{4}+n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{2}+2n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{(4n+1)\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $-2\pi \le x<2\pi .$

- Setting $n=-1$ gives $x=-\frac{3\pi }{2}$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=\frac{\pi }{2}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $-2\pi \le x<2\pi .$ So, the solutions are $x=-\frac{3\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2}.$

Finally, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-\frac{3\pi }{2}+\frac{\pi }{2}=-\pi .
$$
